subject.title: fix(security): narrow sandbox parent to exact active session workspace to prevent cross-agent media read (#107972)

question: Should any agent-scoped media caller retain access to the shared <stateDir>/sandboxes parent when it cannot identify the exact active sandbox workspace?
rationale: The PR treats retaining that parent as backward compatibility, while the canonical security report identifies the same access as the vulnerability; the permanent trust contract requires an explicit owner decision.

options.title: Deny the shared parent
options.body: Remove the broad sandboxes root from all agent-scoped defaults and require affected callers to provide the exact active workspace before sandbox media is authorized.

options.title: Land as partial mitigation
options.body: Narrow only message-action paths, keep https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/107972 open, and explicitly document which remaining callers are intentionally trusted across sessions.

recommendation.title: Deny the shared parent
recommendation.body: Remove the broad sandboxes root from all agent-scoped defaults and require affected callers to provide the exact active workspace before sandbox media is authorized.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent adjacent work on media-root and outbound host-media security makes this the strongest available routing signal.
